x: Tyagaraja was a renounced composer of Carnatic music, a form of Indian classical music. Tyagaraja and his contemporaries, Shyam Shastri and Muthuswami Dikshitai, were regarded as a trinity of Carnatic Music. Tyagaraja composed thousands of devotional compositions, most in Telugu and praise of Lord Rama. He created several new ragas. x: Tyagaraja created new ragas (II) and Annamacharya's sankirtanas praise Lord Venkateswara (IV) are correct. Most Tyagaraja kritis praise Rama, not Krishna (I), and Annamacharya and Tyagaraja were not contemporaries (III), so 'II and IV' is right.

s: Who is the foremost composer of Carnatic music?
x:
Saint Thyagaraja (1767–1847) is regarded as one of the greatest composers of Carnatic music and is revered as a member of the Carnatic Trinity, along with Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri. He composed thousands of devotional Kritis, most of them dedicated to Lord Rama. His compositions are known for their profound devotion, musical excellence and philosophical depth, making them central to the Carnatic music tradition. Although Annamacharya composed over 32,000 Sankirtanas in praise of Lord Venkateswara and is regarded as the Padakavita Pitamaha, the title of the foremost composer of Carnatic music is associated with Saint Thyagaraja. His annual Thyagaraja Aradhana at Tiruvaiyaru continues to attract musicians from across the world. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).
Exam Note:
• Foremost Composer of Carnatic Music – Saint Thyagaraja
• Carnatic Trinity – Thyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, Syama Sastri
• Devotional Deity – Lord Rama
